pages.text: "Time to herd sheep!" Pipo flung open the door and ran out empty-handed. Today he would take sheep to the hilltop. Mom asked, "Pipo, have you packed everything?"

"Yes, all ready!" He crossed the yard. Mom looked beside the door. Scarf, water bottle, and bread bag still hung on pegs. "I do not need them! I want to hurry!" Only his voice came from across the yard.
Grandpa Sheep came to the door, herding sheep with his stick. "The hilltop wind is cold. What if you go without a scarf?" The thought made Pipo shiver, throat dry, tummy rumbling.
Grandpa tapped the door pegs with his stick. "We used to count things here before leaving. Shall we try together?" Mom pointed to all three: scarf, water, bread!
Pipo rose onto tiptoe before the pegs and touched his scarf tip. "Scarf, water, bread!" Grandpa tapped three beats. "These three make you ready for the hill." Mom smiled.
"Now take them down one by one!" Grandpa whispered. First, Pipo took the scarf and wrapped it once around his neck. "One, scarf!" Mom and Grandpa counted with him.
Water bottle in his hand! Bread bag on his shoulder! Everyone counted each item. "Two, water! Three, bread!" The pegs were empty. Pipo called, "Scarf, water, bread—all here!"
Wind whistled at the hilltop, but his scarf was warm. Pipo ate bread as sheep grazed beside him. Crouching, hands at his chest, he said, "Nothing missing!"
The next morning, before Grandpa arrived, Pipo stood alone at the pegs. "One, scarf! Two, water! Three, bread!" He touched and took each one. Empty pegs again. "Scarf, water, bread—all here!"
Mom hugged Pipo close. "All packed by yourself!" Touching the pegs one by one left nothing behind. Burying his face against her neck, he called, "Scarf, water, bread—all here!"
